name: Hong Kong
description: Hong Kong remains a dynamic global financial hub offering significant career opportunities and a unique East-meets-West culture. Despite high living costs, its favorable tax regime and efficient infrastructure continue to attract expats seeking professional growth and a vibrant urban lifestyle.
longdescription: Hong Kong is a Special Administrative Region of China, renowned for its bustling environment and diverse culture, blending traditional Chinese heritage with modern Western influences. It is a major international financial center, attracting expatriates primarily to its finance, legal, and tech sectors, often with competitive salaries and benefits such as housing allowances. The city boasts world-class public transportation, diverse culinary options, and access to unexpected natural escapes like hiking trails and beaches, contributing to a rich lifestyle. However, expats face challenges including an extremely high cost of living, particularly for housing, and often demanding long working hours. The expat community is large and active, making it relatively easy to establish social circles, though some expats report difficulties in forming deep connections with locals. Air quality can be a concern, and while healthcare is world-class, private options can be expensive. Recent years have seen a shift in the talent pool, with an increasing influx of mainland Chinese professionals, making local language skills (Mandarin or Cantonese) increasingly important for career progression and integration in some business contexts.

visas.name: Top Talent Pass Scheme (TTPS)
visas.description: The Top Talent Pass Scheme (TTPS) is an immigration program launched by the Hong Kong government to attract high-earning professionals and graduates from world-renowned universities. It allows eligible individuals to enter Hong Kong without a prior job offer to explore employment or establish a business.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are high-income individuals or graduates from eligible top universities with or without extensive work experience, seeking to work or start a business in Hong Kong.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Persons admitted under the TTPS who have ordinarily resided in the HKSAR for a continuous period of not less than seven years may apply for the right of abode in the HKSAR in accordance with the law.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must demonstrate they have taken up employment in Hong Kong with a stable income (with remuneration at market level) or have established/joined a business in Hong Kong. For extensions under the 'Top-Tier Employment Stream', applicants must have been in Hong Kong for at least two years under TTPS and have an assessable income for salaries tax of not less than HK$2 million in the previous year of assessment.
visas.tax_implications: Holders are subject to Hong Kong income tax requirements. Hong Kong has a low and simple tax system. There are no special tax exemptions specifically for the TTPS, and standard resident tax rules apply.
benefits: No prior job offer required for initial application
Full flexibility to work, change employers, or establish a business in Hong Kong
Spouse and unmarried dependent children under 18 can join on dependent visas with unrestricted work rights
Fast processing time, typically 2-4 weeks
Path to permanent residency after 7 years of ordinary residence
required_documents: Applicant's recent photograph
Valid travel document (passport)
Hong Kong Identity Card (if any)
Official bachelor's degree graduation certificate and transcript (for Categories B and C)
Verification proof of bachelor's degree qualification (for Categories B and C)
Documentary proof of annual individual income of HK$2.5 million or above (for Category A)
Documentary proof of work experience (for Categories B)
application_process_steps: Prepare all required documents, ensuring they are in English or Chinese, or have certified translations.
Submit the application online through the Hong Kong Immigration Department's e-Visa portal.
Upload all supporting documents digitally.
Pay the non-refundable application fee online.
The Immigration Department reviews the application and may request additional documents.
Receive an electronic notification of approval-in-principle; upon arrival, collect the visa label/e-Visa.

visas.name: General Employment Policy (GEP)
visas.description: The General Employment Policy (GEP) in Hong Kong is designed for foreign professionals who possess special skills, knowledge, or experience that are valuable to and not readily available in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR). It is an employer-sponsored scheme allowing such individuals to work and reside in Hong Kong.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-local professional who has a confirmed job offer from a Hong Kong employer, whose skills are not readily available in the local workforce, and who will receive a remuneration package broadly commensurate with market standards.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Individuals admitted under the GEP who have ordinarily resided in the HKSAR for a continuous period of not less than seven years may apply for the right of abode (permanent residency) in accordance with the law.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must continue to meet the eligibility criteria under the GEP. Top-tier entrants (those permitted to take up employment for not less than 2 years and having an assessable income for salaries tax of not less than HK$2 million in the previous year of assessment) may be granted an extension of stay for a period of five years.
benefits: Legal right to work and reside in Hong Kong.
Ability to bring spouse and unmarried dependent children under 18.
Clear pathway to Permanent Residency (PR) after 7 years of continuous ordinary residence.
No sector restrictions (open to all legitimate industries).
required_documents: Completed application form (ID 990A).
Copy of applicant's valid travel document (personal particulars page, and latest arrival stamp/extension of stay label if currently in HKSAR).
Copy of applicant's Hong Kong identity card (if applicable).
Proof of residing abroad (if applicable).
Proof of educational background (e.g., degree certificates, professional qualifications).
Proof of relevant work experience.
Recent passport-sized photograph.
Employment contract or letter of appointment from the employer detailing position, salary, benefits, and employment period.
Copy of the employer's Business Registration Certificate.
Proof of the employer's financial standing (e.g., most recent audited financial report, trading profit and loss statement, or profit tax return).
Documentary evidence demonstrating that the position cannot be readily filled by the local workforce or requires special skills not available locally.
application_process_steps: Check eligibility requirements and confirm the role is professional-level, market-paid, and hard to fill locally.
Gather all required documents from both the applicant and the sponsoring employer.
Submit the visa/entry permit application to the Hong Kong Immigration Department, typically through the official online portal.
Pay the non-refundable application fee (HKD 600) upon submission, and a visa issuance fee (HKD 1,300 for stays over 180 days) upon approval.
Attend any required appointments, interviews, or biometrics sessions, if requested.
Receive the decision and, if approved, activate the visa and prepare for relocation to Hong Kong.

visas.name: Quality Migrant Admission Scheme (QMAS)
visas.description: The Quality Migrant Admission Scheme (QMAS) seeks to attract highly skilled or talented persons to settle in Hong Kong in order to enhance its economic competitiveness. Applicants are not required to have secured an offer of local employment before applying for entry or being admitted to Hong Kong for settlement under the Scheme.
visas.target_applicant: Highly skilled or talented persons who can contribute to Hong Kong's economy and workforce, without requiring a prior job offer.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After living continuously for not less than 7 years in Hong Kong, applicants can apply for the right of abode (permanent residency).
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants admitted through the General Points Test are required to provide proofs demonstrating that they have taken steps to settle in Hong Kong by taking up residence, such as securing gainful employment or establishing a business, to obtain an extension of stay at the end of the initial period.
benefits: No requirement to secure an offer of local employment before applying.
Freedom to take up and change employment during permitted stay without prior approval.
Dependants (spouse and children) are allowed to join.
Pathway to Permanent Residency after 7 years of continuous residence.
Initial stay of 36 months for General Points Test entrants (or 8 years for Achievement-based Points Test entrants).
required_documents: Valid travel document
Recent photograph
Proof of personal net worth
Proof of academic/professional qualifications
Proof of work experience
Proof of income record (if any)
Language proficiency proof
Proof of achievement (for Achievement-based Points Test)
Resume
Reference Letter from the Employer
Evidence of Self-Employment Experience (if applicable)
Evidence of Career Accomplishment (if applicable)
Evidence of Future Plan
application_process_steps: Determine eligibility and choose an assessment route (General Points Test or Achievement-based Points Test).
Gather all necessary supporting documents.
Submit the application online or by post to the Hong Kong Immigration Department.
Attend an interview in Hong Kong if invited by the Immigration Department.
Receive an "Approval-in-Principle" and subsequently a formal visa grant.
Pay the visa fee and collect the e-Visa.
Relocate to Hong Kong and apply for a Hong Kong ID card.

visas.name: New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES)
visas.description: The New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES) is a residency by investment program launched in Hong Kong on March 1, 2024. It aims to attract high-net-worth individuals and capital to Hong Kong by granting them the right to live, work, and study in the region in exchange for a significant capital investment in permissible assets. This scheme contributes to Hong Kong's talent pool and strengthens its asset and wealth management business, financial services, and related professional sectors.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign nationals (excluding Afghanistan, Cuba, and Democratic People's Republic of Korea), Chinese nationals with permanent residency in a foreign country, Macao Special Administrative Region residents, or Chinese residents of Taiwan, who are aged 18 or above, and possess substantial net assets and a clean immigration record.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After a period of continuous ordinary residence in Hong Kong for not less than seven years, the entrant and their dependants may apply to the Director of Immigration for Hong Kong permanent resident status. Alternatively, after seven years of continuously satisfying the financial requirements, an entrant may apply for unconditional stay, which permits entry and stay in Hong Kong without any conditions or limit of stay.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants and their dependants must continue to satisfy the eligibility criteria and requirements of the New CIES. Extensions of stay for not more than three years will normally be granted, and applicants must be physically present in Hong Kong at the time of application for extension.
benefits: Right to live, work, and study in Hong Kong.
Inclusion of spouse/partner and unmarried dependent children under 18.
No requirement to establish or operate a business.
Path to Hong Kong permanent residency after 7 years of continuous ordinary residence.
Investment in a diverse range of permissible asset classes.
required_documents: Passport bio-data page and all used pages.
Birth certificate or household register (for Chinese nationals).
Marriage certificate (if adding spouse).
Birth certificates for each child dependant.
Police clearance certificates from every country of residence for 12+ months during the past 10 years.
Bank statements covering the preceding 24 months (for net asset proof).
Audited financial statements for privately-held companies (if applicable).
Property valuation reports from a HKIS-registered surveyor (if applicable).
Precious metals or collectibles valuation by an accredited appraiser (if applicable).
Certifying Proof for Fulfillment of Net Asset Requirement from InvestHK.
Certifying Proof for Fulfillment of Investment Requirements from InvestHK.
application_process_steps: Applicant applies to the New CIES Office (under InvestHK) for Net Asset Assessment, demonstrating net assets of not less than HKD 30 million held throughout the six months preceding the application.
Upon verification by InvestHK, a Certifying Proof for Fulfillment of Net Asset Requirement is issued. The applicant then submits an entry application to the Immigration Department (ImmD).

If Approval-in-Principle is granted by ImmD, a visa/entry permit is issued for entering Hong Kong on visitor status for up to 180 days to make the committed investment of HKD 30 million in permissible assets.

After making the investment, the applicant seeks verification from the New CIES Office for fulfillment of Investment Requirements and obtains a Certifying Proof. This proof is then submitted to ImmD, leading to formal approval and an initial permission to stay for not more than 24 months.

visas.name: Investment as Entrepreneurs (under GEP)
visas.description: The 'Investment as Entrepreneurs (under GEP)' program is Hong Kong's primary pathway for foreign nationals seeking to establish or join a business in the city. It falls under the General Employment Policy (GEP) and allows individuals to operate a Hong Kong company as a director, shareholder, or both.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is ideal for individuals with relevant industry experience or professional qualifications who plan to incorporate or actively manage a company in Hong Kong and can demonstrate that their business will make a substantial contribution to the local economy.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 7 consecutive years of lawful and ordinary residence in Hong Kong under this visa, applicants and their dependants may apply for the Right of Abode (permanent residency).
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must continue to meet the eligibility criteria for entry for investment, and successful applicants are normally granted extensions following a 3-2 year pattern on employment condition.
visas.tax_implications: Null, as standard Hong Kong tax rules apply, which are generally considered favorable for individuals and businesses.
benefits: Ability to register and operate a Hong Kong company with full ownership rights.
Official residency and identity cards, granting access to local public services like banking, healthcare, and schooling.
Clear path to permanent residency after 7 years of continuous ordinary residence.
Family relocation privileges, allowing sponsorship of spouse and unmarried dependent children under 18.
No statutory minimum capital requirement, with focus on economic contribution and business feasibility.
required_documents: Valid travel document (passport) with at least 6 months validity.
Completed application form (e.g., Form ID(E)1040 mentioned by one source, but official ImmD usually refers to online portal for GEP applications).
Recent passport-style photograph.
Curriculum Vitae (CV).
Proof of academic qualifications (normally a first degree in a relevant field, or good technical qualifications/proven professional abilities and experience).

Detailed three-year business plan with market analysis, market positioning, business direction, sales targets, product marketing strategy, and financial forecasts (profit-and-loss, cash flow, balance sheet).
Proof of personal and company financial standing (bank statements from the previous year, proof of other funding sources, latest audited financial report if any).
Documentary proof of capital investment in Hong Kong, demonstrating ability to support business operations.
Evidence of business premises, such as a signed commercial lease (if applicable).
Company documents (if registered prior to application).
Nomination of a local sponsor (company or individual).
application_process_steps: Ensure eligibility criteria are met, including a clean criminal record and good education background.
Develop a comprehensive three-year business plan and gather all required financial evidence and supporting documents.
Consider incorporating a company in Hong Kong before applying and establish local premises.
Nominate a local sponsor (individual or company).
Submit the application, preferably online through the Hong Kong Immigration Department's official portal.
Pay the non-refundable application fee.
Await approval from the Immigration Department, which typically takes 3-4 weeks upon receipt of all required documents.

visas.name: Student Visa
visas.description: The Hong Kong Student Visa (or Entry Permit) allows non-local students to enter and remain in the HKSAR for a specified program of full-time study at a recognized educational institution. It enables international students to pursue education and provides potential pathways for post-study work and permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an international student who has received an acceptance letter for a full-time, locally accredited post-secondary program or an approved exchange program at a recognized educational institution in Hong Kong.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Student visa holders can apply for Hong Kong Permanent Residency (PR) after 7 years of continuous 'ordinary residence'. This period includes time spent as a student, provided the individual meets the condition of being 'ordinarily resident in Hong Kong' for the majority of the time (at least 183 days per year) and maintains a fixed abode. Many transition to an IANG (Immigration Arrangements for Non-local Graduates) or other work visas after study.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet eligibility criteria, maintain student status, and for dependants, maintain relationship with sponsor and sponsor remains a bona fide Hong Kong resident.
visas.tax_implications: Part-time income earned by student visa holders is taxable, but most students fall within the tax-free allowance (annual income below HK$144,000 is usually fully exempt for 2025-2026).
benefits: Access to world-class universities and globally recognized qualifications.
Opportunity to work part-time during term and full-time during holidays (for eligible students).
Potential pathway to permanent residency after 7 years of ordinary residence.
Exposure to a cosmopolitan environment and industry engagement.
Dependants (spouse and children) may join the student in Hong Kong.
required_documents: Completed application form ID 995A (and ID 995B by sponsor)
Recent passport-size photograph
Photocopy of valid travel document (passport)
Photocopy of Hong Kong identity card (if any)
Letter of acceptance from the education institution
Proof of financial support (e.g., bank statements covering 6 months, savings account passbooks, tax receipts, salary slips, scholarship award letters, loan approval letters)
Proof of accommodation arrangements (especially for applicants under 18)
English language proficiency scores (e.g., IELTS or TOEFL) (if applicable)
Academic transcripts/Highest Public Examination/Academic Result
Consent letter from a parent authorizing a guardian (if under 18)
Sponsorship letter from parents/guardian/institution (if applicable)
application_process_steps: Obtain an acceptance letter from a recognized educational institution in Hong Kong.
Nominate a local sponsor (either the educational institution or an individual over 18 who is a bona fide Hong Kong resident).
Complete application form ID 995A and have your sponsor complete ID 995B.
Gather all required supporting documents, including proof of financial support, valid travel document, and academic records.
Submit the application either online via the GovHK website, by post to the Immigration Department, or often through the sponsoring university.
Pay the prescribed visa application fee upon instruction from the immigration department (usually HKD 230).
Await processing; typically within 6 weeks, but can extend to 8-10 weeks during peak seasons.
Receive the e-Visa/No Objection Letter (NOL) upon approval, print it, and present it upon entry to Hong Kong.

visas.name: Dependant Visa / Family Sponsorship Visa
visas.description: The Hong Kong Dependant Visa is designed for immediate family members of eligible visa holders or Hong Kong permanent residents to join them for residence in Hong Kong. This visa allows for family reunification, enabling spouses, legally recognized partners, and unmarried dependent children to live in the Special Administrative Region.
visas.target_applicant: Immediate family members (spouse, other party to an eligible registered relationship, and unmarried dependent children under 18) of individuals holding valid employment, investment, or talent scheme visas, or Hong Kong permanent residents. Parents aged 60 or above can also be sponsored if the sponsor is a Hong Kong permanent resident.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Persons admitted for residence as dependants who have ordinarily resided in the HKSAR for a continuous period of not less than seven years may apply for the right of abode in the HKSAR (permanent residency) in accordance with the law.
visas.renewal_conditions: Dependants may apply for an extension of stay provided they continue to meet the eligibility criteria, the sponsor remains a bona fide Hong Kong resident (employee/investor), the relationship remains valid, and the sponsor continues to meet financial and accommodation requirements. The length of renewed stay will typically align with the sponsor's visa duration. For specified schemes, extensions of stay within three months before expiry are advised.
benefits: Allows family reunification in Hong Kong.
Dependants are generally permitted to work or study in Hong Kong without needing to obtain a separate visa (with an exception for dependants of student visa holders).
Provides a pathway to permanent residency in Hong Kong after a continuous period of ordinary residence.
Children can attend local or international schools, providing educational continuity.
required_documents: Completed Application Form ID 997 (Parts A and B, for dependant and sponsor respectively)
Applicant's valid travel document (passport) with personal particulars, issue/expiry dates, and any Hong Kong visa/entry stamp (if applicable)
Applicant's recent passport-sized photograph
Applicant's Hong Kong Identity Card (if previously issued)
Proof of relationship with the sponsor (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate, adoption papers, family photographs, family letters)
Sponsor's valid travel document (passport) with personal details page and current Hong Kong visa/entry permit/extension of stay label (if not a permanent resident)
Sponsor's Hong Kong Identity Card
Proof of sponsor's financial standing (e.g., recent bank statements, employment contract, salary slips, tax assessment or income proof)
Proof of sponsor's accommodation in Hong Kong (e.g., tenancy agreement, rental receipts, property ownership documents)
Additional supporting evidence may be requested to demonstrate a genuine relationship
application_process_steps: Prepare all required documents for both the sponsor and the dependant, ensuring all necessary supporting evidence is ready.
Complete and sign the official Application Form ID 997 (Parts A for dependant, B for sponsor).
Submit the application and supporting documents to the Hong Kong Immigration Department. This can be done online, by post, or through a Chinese Embassy/Consulate if the dependant is overseas.
The Immigration Department will assess the application and may request additional documents or clarifications.

Upon approval of the visa/entry permit, pay the required visa fee. For most non-specified scheme applications, this fee is HK$330 payable upon approval. For applications under 'Specified Schemes', a non-refundable application fee of HK$600 and a visa issuance fee (HK$600 for stays up to 180 days, HK$1,300 for stays over 180 days) are required upon submission.
Once the visa is issued, collect the e-Visa and apply for a Hong Kong Identity Card at a Registration of Persons Office upon arrival or approval if not already holding one.

visas.name: Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals (ASMTP)
visas.description: The Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals (ASMTP) is a Hong Kong immigration program designed to attract qualified Chinese residents of the Mainland who possess special skills, knowledge, or experience valuable to and not readily available in the HKSAR. It aims to meet local manpower needs and enhance Hong Kong's competitiveness in the global market, allowing them to work in Hong Kong under an employer-sponsored arrangement.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are Chinese residents of the Mainland with a bachelor's degree or higher, or relevant technical qualifications and proven professional abilities, who have a confirmed offer of employment in Hong Kong for a role relevant to their expertise that cannot be readily filled by the local workforce.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Persons admitted under the ASMTP who have ordinarily resided in the HKSAR for a continuous period of not less than seven years may apply for the right of abode (permanent residency) in the HKSAR in accordance with the law.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must continue to meet the eligibility criteria under the ASMTP. For 'top-tier entrants' seeking more favorable extensions, they must have been permitted to work under ASMTP for at least two years and have an assessable income for salaries tax of not less than HK$2 million in the previous year of assessment.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Hong Kong salaries tax rules apply. For extension purposes, individuals seeking 'top-tier entrant' status must have an assessable income for salaries tax of not less than HK$2 million in the previous year of assessment.
benefits: Quota-free and non-sector specific, unlike some other schemes.
Dependants (spouse and unmarried children under 18) can also obtain visas and are permitted to work in Hong Kong without a separate work visa.
Offers a potential path to permanent residency in Hong Kong after ordinarily residing for a continuous period of not less than seven years.
Remuneration packages are required to be broadly commensurate with prevailing market levels for professionals in the HKSAR.
Initial stay of 36 months, providing a substantial period for employment and settlement.
required_documents: Completed application form (ID 990A for applicant, ID 990B for dependants if applicable)
Copy of valid travel document (e.g., PRC passport, Exit-entry Permit for Travelling to and from Hong Kong and Macao (EEP))
Copy of previous travel document pages showing any previous visa/entry permit labels or landing slips in HKSAR (if applicable)

Academic certificates and proof of professional qualifications (normally a first degree in the relevant field, or good technical qualifications, proven professional abilities, and/or relevant experience and achievements)
A confirmed offer of employment in Hong Kong, including the employment contract or formal offer letter (specifying role, salary, benefits, and start date)
Supporting documents from the employing company in Hong Kong (e.g., business registration certificate, financial reports, detailed business plan for newly established companies)
Job description and justification for why the position cannot be readily filled by the local workforce
Proof of specialized skills/qualifications relevant to the job offer
Recent passport-style photo(s)
application_process_steps: The Hong Kong employer prepares a genuine, full-time job offer with market-aligned salary and employment terms.
The employer gathers corporate documents (e.g., business registration, financial proof) and a justification for hiring a non-local talent.
The applicant (or employer on their behalf) submits the application online with all required supporting documents to the Hong Kong Immigration Department.
The Immigration Department processes the application, normally taking four weeks upon receipt of all required documents and the relevant application fee.
Upon approval, an 'e-Visa' entry permit is issued, and the applicant pays the visa issuance fee (HK$600 for stay up to 180 days, HK$1,300 for stay of 181 days or more).

Successful applicants who are Chinese residents of the Mainland must then apply for an Exit-entry Permit for Travelling to and from Hong Kong and Macao (EEP) and a relevant exit endorsement from the Mainland authorities before travelling to Hong Kong.

visas.name: Immigration Arrangements for Non-local Graduates (IANG)
visas.description: The Immigration Arrangements for Non-local Graduates (IANG) program is a Hong Kong immigration scheme designed to attract and retain non-local talent who have graduated from a full-time, locally-accredited program in Hong Kong or from a Hong Kong university's campus in the Greater Bay Area. It allows eligible graduates to stay and work in the HKSAR.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-local student who has obtained an undergraduate or higher qualification from a full-time, locally-accredited program in Hong Kong or from an eligible Greater Bay Area campus, and wishes to stay or return to work in Hong Kong.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Non-Chinese nationals may apply for the Right of Abode (permanent residency) after ordinarily residing in Hong Kong continuously for not less than seven years. Time spent in Hong Kong as a student before obtaining the IANG visa can count towards this seven-year period, provided the residence was continuous and ordinary.
visas.renewal_conditions: For extension of stay, applicants must have secured an offer of employment or established/joined a business in Hong Kong. The job must be at a level commonly taken up by degree holders and the remuneration package should be at market level. Eligible top-tier entrants (those with an assessable income for salaries tax of not less than HK$2 million in the previous year of assessment) may be granted an extension of stay for six years.
benefits: Quota-free and non-sector specific, offering broad employment opportunities.
Non-local recent graduates (applying within six months of graduation) do not require a job offer upon application.
Holders are generally free to take up and change employment during their permitted stay without prior approval.
Provides a clear path to permanent residency in Hong Kong.
Allows for an initial stay of 24 months on time limitation only, without other conditions of stay.
required_documents: Valid travel document (and previous travel document if applicable)
Hong Kong identity card (if already held as a former student)
Official transcript of academic records
Graduation certificate or supporting letter from the degree awarding institution showing attainment of undergraduate or higher qualification
For non-local non-recent graduates: Company's employment contract or letter of appointment to the applicant, stating position, remuneration, and duration of employment
For non-local recent graduates without a job offer: Proof of financial means to support self during initial stay (e.g., bank statements, sponsor letter)
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility as a non-local recent graduate or non-recent graduate.
Assemble all required supporting documents.
Create an account on the IANG online portal (gov.hk/iang).
Complete the online application form and upload all supporting documents.
Pay the non-refundable application fee of HK$600 via the online portal.
Wait for the application to be processed (approximately two weeks for recent graduates).
Upon approval, pay the visa issuance fee (HK$1,300 for the initial 24-month visa).
Download the e-Visa and either print it or save it digitally.

visas.name: Admission Scheme for the Second Generation of Chinese Hong Kong Permanent Residents
visas.description: This scheme encourages the second generation of Chinese Hong Kong permanent residents who have emigrated overseas to return to work in the HKSAR. It provides an opportunity for individuals with family ties to Hong Kong to live and work in the region, contributing to its social, economic, and cultural development.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are Chinese nationals aged 18-40, born overseas, with at least one parent holding a valid Hong Kong Permanent Identity Card and who was a Chinese national settled overseas at the time of the applicant's birth, possessing a good education background, proficiency in Chinese or English, and sufficient financial means.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Persons admitted under this Scheme who have ordinarily resided in the HKSAR for a continuous period of not less than seven years may apply for the right of abode in the HKSAR in accordance with the law.
visas.renewal_conditions: Successful applicants for extension of stay are normally permitted to remain on time limitation on a 3-3 year extension pattern without other conditions of stay. For a 'top-tier employment stream' extension, applicants must have been permitted to remain for not less than two years and have an assessable income for salaries tax of not less than HK$2 million in the previous year of assessment.
benefits: Freedom to take up or change employment without prior approval.
Freedom to establish or join in business without prior approval.
Initial stay of 24 months with possibility of extension.
Pathway to permanent residency after 7 years of ordinary residence.
Dependants are allowed to join the applicant in Hong Kong.
required_documents: Recent Photograph
Travel Document
Evidence of the applicant's relationship with his/her Chinese Hong Kong Permanent Resident parent(s) (e.g., applicant's birth certificate)
Valid Hong Kong Permanent Identity Card of applicant's parent(s)
Proof of academic qualifications and relevant work experience
Applicant's financial standing
application_process_steps: Meet the eligibility criteria, including age, birth location, parental status, education, language proficiency, and financial means.
Prepare all required supporting documents.
Submit the application and upload all supporting documents online via the designated GovHK website.
Pay the relevant application fee (if applicable).
Await processing by the Immigration Department.
Applicants can enquire about their application status online or through a 24-hour telephone enquiry system.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Individuals born within the PRC automatically receive Chinese nationality at birth if at least one parent is a Chinese national. Children born abroad to at least one Chinese parent are also Chinese nationals, unless they hold foreign citizenship at birth and the Chinese-national parent has acquired either permanent residency overseas or foreign citizenship.

Naturalization.desc: Foreigners wishing to acquire Chinese nationality (as Hong Kong does not have its own separate citizenship) must apply for naturalization under the Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China. Key requirements include holding Hong Kong Permanent Residency (Right of Abode), which typically requires seven continuous years of ordinary residence, being willing to renounce any other nationality (as China does not allow dual citizenship), demonstrating close ties to Hong Kong (e.g., family, business, property, long-term employment), and having a clear criminal record. Applications are assessed rigorously on a case-by-case basis.

Birthright.desc: Chinese nationals born in Hong Kong automatically become permanent residents. Foreign nationals born in Hong Kong can become permanent residents if at least one parent holds the Right of Abode in Hong Kong.

Spouse and Family.desc: Having a close relative who is a Chinese national can be a legitimate reason for naturalization. Specific factors that can improve chances for naturalization include being married to a Chinese (Hong Kong Resident), having children born in Hong Kong, and having a spouse and minor children residing in Hong Kong.

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax (Salaries Tax):** Hong Kong operates a territorial tax system, meaning only income arising in or derived from Hong Kong is taxed. Salaries tax is levied on net chargeable income at progressive rates from 2% to 17% or at a standard rate of 15% on assessable income less personal deductions, whichever is lower. With effect from the 2024-25 tax year, there are two-tiered standard rates: 15% on the first HKD 5 million of assessable income (less personal deductions) and 16% on the portion exceeding HKD 5 million. A basic allowance of HKD 132,000 is available.
*   **Corporate Tax (Profits Tax):** The standard corporate tax rate is 16.5%. A reduced rate of 8.25% applies to the first HKD 2 million of assessable profits, with profits exceeding this amount taxed at the standard 16.5%.
*   **Value-Added Tax (VAT) / Sales Tax:** Hong Kong does not levy VAT, goods and services tax, or sales tax.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** There is no capital gains tax in Hong Kong.
*   **Dividend Tax:** Hong Kong does not tax dividends.
*   **Property Tax:** Charged annually at a standard rate of 15% on the net assessable value of land or buildings, after a 20% notional allowance. Rental income derived by a corporation from Hong Kong property is subject to profits tax.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Hong Kong is consistently ranked among the most expensive cities globally, primarily due to extremely high rental costs. Expect to pay significantly for accommodation, especially in central expat areas like Mid-Levels or Discovery Bay.
*   **Language:** While English is widely spoken in business and among the expat community, learning some basic Cantonese or Mandarin can greatly enhance daily life and professional opportunities, especially given the increasing influence of mainland Chinese businesses.
*   **Safety:** Hong Kong generally has low crime rates and is considered a very safe city, even at night. However, vigilance, as in any major city, is always recommended.
*   **Registration:** Any individual aged 11 or above intending to reside in Hong Kong for more than 180 days must apply for a Hong Kong Identity Card (HKID) within 30 days of arrival.
*   **Transportation:** The public transportation system is highly efficient, affordable, and extensive, including MTR, buses, and ferries, making commuting relatively easy.
*   **Healthcare:** Hong Kong offers world-class healthcare. While the public system is subsidized, many expats opt for private healthcare, which can be expensive without international health insurance.
